title: Stable matchings of teachers to schools
extended_summary:
This paper studies the computational properties of assigning teachers to schools in a centralized matching system. The motivation comes from teacher labor markets in which teachers specialize in two subjects and schools have subject-specific staffing capacities. The central question is whether stable assignments exist under different preference structures and, when they do not, how hard it is to find the most stable assignment.

The authors formalize the Teachers Assignment Problem (TAP), define two notions of blocking pairs/stability, and analyze several variants. In the basic variant, teachers rank schools and schools rank applicants; in the subject-specific variant, schools can rank applicants differently by subject. The paper proves NP-completeness for the existence of a stable matching in the general case, but shows polynomial-time solvability when preferences are generated by a master list of applicants or a master list of schools.

The paper is purely theoretical and uses reductions from satisfiability problems rather than empirical data. It also proves that finding a matching with the minimum number of blocking pairs is strongly inapproximable unless P=NP, for both TAP variants. The results are positioned as characterizing the boundary between tractable and intractable versions of teacher-to-school matching with subject constraints.

identified_tools.description: A general classroom/education matching or assignment algorithmic system, not an AI tutoring or feedback product.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper studies the computational problem of assigning teachers to schools under stable matching constraints, including variants with master lists and subject-specific preferences. It does not evaluate an AI coaching or lesson-feedback tool.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/computational matching paper, not an empirical study of an AI educational tool or coaching system. It contains no intervention, usage, or outcome evidence related to teacher coaching or lesson-plan feedback.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational AI tool impact is measured or reported. The paper addresses algorithmic tractability of teacher-school assignments rather than instructional outcomes.
